s1-wall: Vertical portrait night photograph taken from standing eye level looking straight at a patch of faded Victorian bedroom wallpaper by candlelight with faint pencil handwriting scrawled low on the wall, indistinct scratchy words, a woman's shadow of a hand holding a candle at the edge of frame. Picture rail at the top of frame, skirting board at the bottom. No people, no readable letters. Cold, desaturated, heavy film grain, deep shadow.
s2-rectory: Vertical portrait night photograph taken from standing eye level looking straight at a tall gaunt Victorian red-brick rectory at night behind an overgrown hedge, many dark windows, one dim lamp in a ground-floor room. Night sky at the top of frame, unkempt lawn at the bottom. No people. Cold, desaturated, heavy film grain, deep shadow.
s3-nun: Vertical portrait night photograph taken from standing eye level looking straight down an overgrown garden path at dusk toward a distant small figure in a dark nun's habit walking away between hedges, far off, features indistinct, almost silhouette. Trees at the top of frame, gravel path at the bottom. Face never visible. Cold, desaturated, heavy film grain, very dark.
s4-fire: Vertical portrait night photograph taken from standing eye level looking straight at the Victorian rectory at night with firelight glowing orange from inside its windows and smoke rising against the dark sky, seen from the garden. Night sky and smoke at the top of frame, dark lawn at the bottom. No people, no flames outside the windows. Cold night, desaturated apart from the window glow, heavy film grain.
s5-churchyard: Vertical portrait night photograph taken from standing eye level looking straight across an old English churchyard at dusk, leaning gravestones, a square-towered flint church, mist low over the grass, an empty field beyond where a garden once was. Grey sky at the top of frame, long wet grass at the bottom. No people. Cold, desaturated, heavy film grain, deep shadow.
